forces.title: Volatile Crude Oil Prices Due to Geopolitical Instability
forces.description: The ongoing 'stop-start' US-Iran conflict and broader West Asian volatility lead to significant fluctuations in Brent crude oil prices. This volatility translates into higher energy costs for manufacturing and logistics within the Gems, Jewellery & Luxury Goods sector, compressing profit margins. Currency depreciation against the USD, exacerbated by high oil prices, further increases import costs for raw materials, impacting overall profitability.

forces.title: Gold Consumption Shifts from Jewellery to Investment
forces.description: India's gold consumption is undergoing a fundamental change, with jewellery's share falling below 60% of total purchases in CY25 compared to a long-term average of 70%. Investment demand, driven by geopolitical uncertainty, sustained gold price rallies, and portfolio diversification, now accounts for 42% of consumption. This structural shift requires jewellers to adapt their product offerings and marketing strategies to cater to evolving consumer priorities.
forces.source_title: India’s Gold Consumption Rises to Record 40 pct in CY25

forces.title: Government Support and Liberal FDI Policy Boosting Sector Growth
forces.description: India's Gems & Jewellery sector benefits from 100% FDI under the automatic route, special economic zones (SEZs) contributing 30% to total exports, and favorable trade agreements like CEPA with UAE and ECTA with Australia. These policies attract foreign investment, enhance export competitiveness by eliminating tariffs, and support manufacturing units, creating a conducive environment for both domestic and international players to expand their presence and boost overall sector growth.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

forces.title: Rising Demand for Lab-Grown Diamonds and Customised Jewellery
forces.description: The emergence of lab-grown diamonds, championed by brands like 'beYon' (Titan) and 'Ethera' (BlueStone), is creating new market opportunities, particularly for affordable, everyday-wear jewellery. Alongside this, a growing consumer preference for customised designs (e.g., Malabar Gold) indicates a shift towards personalized luxury. These trends drive innovation and diversification in product offerings, attracting a broader consumer base and fostering new investment in the sector.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

forces.title: Accelerated Formalisation and Store Expansion by Branded Jewellers
forces.description: Organised jewellery retailers are aggressively expanding their retail footprint, adding hundreds of new stores, often through franchisee models to optimize inventory funding. This expansion, coupled with consumer preferences shifting towards branded players due to regulatory interventions (like mandatory hallmarking), is driving market share gains for formal sector players. This leads to robust revenue growth and increased efficiency, strengthening the overall organised jewellery market.
forces.source_title: India’s Gold Consumption Rises to Record 40 pct in CY25

forces.title: Increasing Digital Adoption and Omnichannel Retail Strategies
forces.description: Jewellery retailers are re-evaluating traditional business models by implementing omnichannel approaches with a strong focus on digital strategy. This includes online selling platforms and innovative virtual reality (VR) experiences for customers, allowing them to view and customize jewellery digitally. This shift caters to evolving consumer shopping habits, expands market reach, and enhances customer engagement, signifying a crucial modernization of the retail landscape within the sector.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

forces.title: Rising Gold Prices Boosting Jeweller Profitability Through Inventory Gains
forces.description: Elevated and volatile gold prices, driven by structural demand shifts and macroeconomic conditions, have led to significant inventory gains for jewellers holding unhedged gold. This is expected to expand average gross profit margins, with CareEdge Ratings projecting a 170-200 bps increase in FY26. While these gains may normalize in FY27, they provide a strong short-term boost to profitability, supporting overall financial health during expansion phases.
forces.source_title: India’s Gold Consumption Rises to Record 40 pct in CY25

forces.title: Increased Inventory Requirements Due to High Gold Prices and Store Expansion
forces.description: Sustained high gold prices combined with aggressive new store additions by jewellers are leading to a marked increase in inventory holding requirements. The median inventory holding days rose significantly in H1 FY26, necessitating increased working capital funding. While franchisee-led expansion helps mitigate debt reliance, the overall funding needs are growing, potentially straining capital structures despite higher profitability from inventory gains, requiring careful financial management.
forces.source_title: India’s Gold Consumption Rises to Record 40 pct in CY25

forces.title: Growing Middle Class and Affluent Consumers Drive Demand
forces.description: India's growing middle class and affluent consumer segments are projected to account for a significantly larger share of total spending by 2036. This demographic shift, coupled with rising disposable incomes, fuels demand for luxury goods, including gems, jewellery, and luxury accessories. This broad-based increase in purchasing power supports market expansion, premiumization trends, and overall consumption growth within the sector.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

forces.title: Rupee Depreciation Amplifies Import Costs for Raw Materials
forces.description: The conflict-driven spikes in global crude prices have led to the Indian Rupee (INR) weakening against the USD, reaching historic lows. This currency depreciation directly increases the landed rupee prices of imported raw materials such as rough diamonds and gold bars, which are critical inputs for India's Gems, Jewellery & Luxury Goods manufacturing sector. Higher import costs can compress profit margins and necessitate adjustments in pricing strategies.

forces.title: Mandatory Hallmarking and BIS Standards Boost Consumer Trust
forces.description: Government initiatives like mandatory BIS hallmarking for gold jewellery, including the BIS logo, purity, and a unique HUID number, enhance authenticity, traceability, and quality assurance. These measures, along with the Safety of Household, Commercial and Similar Electrical Appliances (Quality Control) Order for consumer durables, improve product quality and consumer safety. For the Gems & Jewellery sector, this builds significant consumer trust, encouraging purchases and formalizing the market.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

forces.title: India's Gold and Diamond Trade Contributes Significantly to GDP and Employment
forces.description: As of January 2026, India's gold and diamond trade contributes 7% to the country's GDP and generates skilled and semi-skilled employment for over 50 lakh individuals. This substantial economic contribution underscores the sector's strategic importance and its robust foundation for continued growth. Such a large and entrenched industry is well-positioned to leverage government support and benefit from policy initiatives aimed at economic development and job creation.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

forces.title: Growth in Gold ETFs and Investment Products
forces.description: Inflows into Gold ETFs increased significantly in early 2026, reflecting continued investor preference for gold-backed investment products. This strong growth in investor demand for gold ETFs, with AUM rising substantially, highlights gold's increasing appeal as an asset class. For the Gems & Jewellery sector, this means a broader engagement with gold, even if not directly through physical jewellery, which can still support the underlying gold prices and market sentiment.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Indian Gems & Jewellery Market to Expand Significantly by 2030
viewpoints.description: India’s Gems & Jewellery market is valued at US$ 85 billion as of January 2026 and is projected to grow to US$ 130 billion by 2030. This growth is driven by strong domestic demand, increasing investments, and supportive government policies such as 100% FDI and SEZs. The sector's substantial contribution to GDP and employment underscores its robust growth trajectory and future potential.
viewpoints.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Government Aims for US$100 Billion in Jewellery Exports by 2027
viewpoints.description: The Government of India has set an ambitious target of achieving US$ 100 billion in jewellery exports by 2027, a significant increase from US$ 35 billion in 2020. This objective is supported by various policy measures, including the revised SEZ Act, and free trade agreements like the India-UAE CEPA and India-UK ECTA, which provide duty-free access and enhance global competitiveness for Indian exporters.
viewpoints.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Organised Jewellery Retailers Poised for Strong Revenue Growth in FY26-27
viewpoints.description: Domestic organised jewellery retailers are projected to achieve over 35% revenue growth in FY26 and 20-25% in FY27. This positive outlook is fueled by sustained consumer appetite for jewellery despite rising gold prices, significant market-share gains from accelerated sector formalisation, and aggressive store expansion initiatives. Inventory gains in FY26 will also contribute to expanded operating profit margins.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Gold Consumption Rises to Record 40 pct in CY25

viewpoints.title: Gold Consumption Shifts to Investment, Challenging Traditional Jewellery Demand
viewpoints.description: India's gold consumption patterns are undergoing a structural shift, with jewellery's share falling below 60% of total purchases in CY25 from a long-term average of 70%. Investment demand, driven by geopolitical uncertainty, gold price momentum, and portfolio diversification, is projected to remain strong at 35-40% of overall gold consumption in FY27. This shift signals evolving consumer behavior.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Gold Consumption Rises to Record 40 pct in CY25

viewpoints.title: Lab-Grown Diamond Segment Shows Significant Growth Potential and Investment
viewpoints.description: The lab-grown diamond jewellery segment in India is experiencing rapid growth, attracting substantial investment from both venture capital and established players. Companies like ONYA, BlueStone (via Ethera), and Titan (with beYon) are expanding into this category, focusing on affordable, everyday-wear jewellery and omnichannel growth. This indicates a new, high-potential segment disrupting traditional diamond jewellery.
viewpoints.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Digital Transformation and Omnichannel Strategy Key for Jewellery Retailers
viewpoints.description: Indian jewellery players are actively re-evaluating traditional brick-and-mortar models, shifting towards omnichannel approaches with a strong focus on digital strategy to boost sales. Initiatives like virtual reality (VR) experiences by PC Jewellers, PNG Jewellers, and Popley and Sons are aimed at enhancing customer engagement and experience, reflecting the industry's adaptation to technological advancements and evolving consumer preferences.
viewpoints.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Indian Economy Resilient to Geopolitical Risks and Weak Monsoon for FY27
viewpoints.description: Despite persistent risks from the West Asia crisis and initial monsoon deficits, CareEdge Ratings maintains India's GDP growth projection at 6.7% for FY27. Improved services exports, remittances, and robust capital flows are expected to lead to a Balance of Payments surplus. This macroeconomic resilience provides a stable foundation for discretionary spending sectors like Gems, Jewellery & Luxury Goods, mitigating external shocks.
